name: com.govseer/compliance
title: Govseer
description: Product compliance checks: EU CLP labels, green claims, Amazon claims, CPSC labs and HTS, US DOT

tools.name: check_clp_label
tools.description: Checks the label elements of a hazardous chemical product (signal word, GHS pictograms, H/EUH and P statement codes, product identifier, "Contains" line) against the EU CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008: required elements, pictograms and signal word each hazard statement calls for, precedence rules, the number of P statements, unknown codes. Each finding cites its article. Give the codes as printed on the label or in section 2 of the safety data sheet.

signal_word.description: As printed, e.g. "Danger" or "Warning". Omit if none.

precautionary_statements.description: P codes, single or combined, e.g. ["P280", "P305+P351+P338"].

product_identifier.description: Trade name or substance name as on the label.

contains.description: For mixtures: substances named on the label (Art. 18(3)(b)).

substance.description: True for a single substance, false or omitted for a mixture.

sold_to_general_public.description: True when sold to consumers (nominal quantity then required).

tools.name: clp_statement_wording
tools.description: Returns the official wording of EU CLP hazard (H, EUH) and precautionary (P) statements in any of the 24 EU languages, as published in the consolidated CLP Regulation on EUR-Lex. "…" marks a part the supplier fills in (e.g. the substance or the disposal route).

tools.name: scan_green_claims
tools.description: Scans product page or advert text for environmental claims the EU bans since 27 September 2026 (Directive (EU) 2024/825: generic claims such as "eco-friendly" without recognised excellence, climate-neutral claims based on offsetting) and, for hazardous products, statements CLP keeps off labels and online offers ("non-toxic", "harmless"…). Matches the official examples in the EU languages; each finding cites its source.

text.description: The product page, listing or advert text.

hazardous.description: True when the product is classified hazardous under CLP.

languages.description: Languages of the text. Default: all.

tools.name: scan_amazon_listing
tools.description: Finds pesticide-type claims in an Amazon US product title or description ("kills germs", "disinfects", "repels insects", "prevents mold", "anti-allergen"…). Amazon treats such products as pesticides, which need an EPA registration number or a FIFRA exemption; the scan also lists any EPA registration or establishment numbers it sees.

tools.name: us_limited_quantity
tools.description: Whether US ground shipments of a hazardous material may use the limited quantity exception (49 CFR part 173: 173.150-173.155, 173.306 for aerosols), with the inner packaging limit and the 30 kg package limit, for a hazard class or division and packing group from section 14 of a safety data sheet. The exception applies only where column 8A of the Hazardous Materials Table lists it for the UN entry, and not by air.

tools.name: cpsc_lab_lookup
tools.description: Looks up a testing laboratory on CPSC's list of accepted labs, by CPSC lab ID or by name (exact, or every word of it), and returns the rules (16 CFR parts and standards) it is accepted for. A children's product certificate needs a lab accepted for each rule it was tested to.

name.description: Lab name as on the report.

tools.name: cpsc_hts_flag
tools.description: Returns CPSC's eFiling flag for 10-digit HTS codes: CP2 (certificate data required) or CP1 (may be needed), with CPSC's product category. Not on the list does not mean no certificate is needed; the importer must eFile whenever a certificate is required.

tools.name: upcoming_rules
tools.description: Coming and recent changes to EU CLP, OSHA HCS, WHMIS, Quebec French-language, CPSC eFiling and Amazon dangerous-goods rules, each with its date, state (pending, upcoming, since) and the official source it was checked against.

products.description: Areas: hazard-labels (EU CLP), amazon, sds-gap (OSHA HCS, WHMIS), quebec-label, cpsc. Default: all.
